title: Creamy Chicken Penne Alfredo
seoTitle: Creamy Chicken Penne Alfredo | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Grilled chicken strips in garlic-Parmesan cream sauce for ten
subtitle: Grilled chicken strips in garlic-Parmesan cream sauce for ten
description: Chicken breasts season and sear, then slice into strips. Penne tosses with a stabilized garlic-Parmesan cream sauce and finishes with parsley and cracked pepper.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Creamy Chicken Penne Alfredo in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook the penne
steps.instruction: Boil penne in salted water until al dente, about 10 minutes. Reserve 2 cups pasta water before draining. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.instruction: Season chicken with salt and pepper. Sear in olive oil over medium-high heat 6–7 minutes per side until internal temp reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes and slice. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.instruction: Melt butter in a large pot, sauté garlic 1 minute. Pour in warmed cream and simmer gently 3 minutes—do not boil hard. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk in Parmesan until melted and smooth. Thin with pasta water if too thick. Season with pepper. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.instruction: Add penne and sliced chicken to sauce off heat. Toss until coated. Garnish with parsley and serve immediately or hold warm. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Nutmeg pinch in cream sauce adds depth without changing the classic profile.
Broccoli florets blanched and folded in at the end makes this a full plate.
If sauce tightens on hold, loosen with reserved pasta water, not more cream.
tonightSpread: Alfredo with garlic bread and a simple mixed green salad.
Extra cracked black pepper and Parmesan at the line.
leftovers: Reheat gently with pasta water in a covered pan on low heat.
Bake leftovers in a dish topped with mozzarella for quick alfredo bake.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Alfredo night feels like a treat without leaving the hall. Chicken adds protein crews expect, and the sauce stays silky when held properly in a warm pan.
mealPrepNotes: Warm cream before adding to the pan to reduce curdling risk. Reserve pasta water—it saves a broken sauce. Slice chicken after resting so juices stay in the meat.
